_: Tools section on the home page. build.mjs renders it into <!--#tools-->. 'used' lists project slugs from the research notes in inventory/work/ ('site' = this site). Check a new entry against the project's repo before adding it.
groups: Every page here is designed first, so it can be seen and changed before anything is built.
Licensed type, served the way the licence allows.
Fast pages that still work for someone arriving from a search link.
For the parts of a page that respond as you use them.
Mostly-text sites that send almost no JavaScript to the phone.
Forms and data handled on the server, so they work on a slow connection.
A quick build for small moving pieces on an otherwise plain page.
Styles kept next to the markup, so changing one page doesn't break another.
Print-ready books built from the same text as the website.
Pages load from close to whoever's visiting, and one small server handles forms, payments and email.
Plain servers in Europe for sites with a real database behind them.
Runs the database and search on servers we control.
Hosting for a Next.js front end that has to be quick everywhere.
A plain, well-understood database for anything with real records in it.
Database changes written down as files, so each one can be reviewed.
Keeps busy pages quick by remembering answers for a short while.
Search that copes with typos and half-remembered names.
A small database for sign-ups, close to the site that uses it.
Remembers which payment messages have been handled, so an order is never processed twice.
Open-source maps, so a map page doesn't depend on someone else's pricing.
Card details go straight to Stripe and never touch our server.
Order and enquiry emails sent from your own domain, without touching your inbox setup.
A spam check on forms that doesn't make people solve puzzles.
Tests that fail loudly when a price or a rule changes by mistake.
A real browser that opens every page at phone size and checks it.
Tells us when something breaks for a visitor, so they don't have to.
